Erin —

Thanks for the rollup. Quick read attached a short cheatsheet that contrasts the two paths and a preliminary estimate. High-level summary up front: 

1) Dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated) — fastest to production with predictable throughput and minimal onboarding. Good if you want to avoid networking setup and keep Redwood-managed infra. Typical lead time: 2–4 weeks to reserve and validate capacity, dependent on availability in us-west.

2) Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) — required when customers insist on customer-managed networking or have strict data residency/air-gap requirements. Lead time: 6–10 weeks for VPC control plane + infra provisioning; on-prem longer. Engineering handoffs and security review add time.

Preliminary sizing guidance (from the conservative/aggressive columns in your spreadsheet):
- Conservative pilot: ~8 A40-equivalent GPUs for Dedicated; equivalent private cluster 4–6 nodes (A40 equiv) with reserved headroom for bursting.
- Aggressive pilot: ~24 A40-equivalent GPUs Dedicated; private: 12–18 nodes depending on batch latency needs and KV cache sizing.

I put an approximate monthly unit-cost range in the attached PDF (ballpark only).

Next steps I suggest: 
- Marissa will own cost/contract options and provide committed vs burst pricing.
- Karthik will produce a one-page ops runbook showing how we route fallbacks and KV cache behavior for isolated fleets.
- If you want a Private path, we’ll loop in Vivek to outline security artifacts and lead times.

I’ll follow up with a short proposed SOW.

— Ava Chen
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Erin —

I sketched a short ops comparison below focused on control plane, KV/cache, and latency implications for each hosting posture.

Dedicated (Redwood-managed):
- Control plane: Redwood manages kernels, autoscaling, and routing. We provide per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdowns.
- KV cache: Shared prefix cache is possible across tenants; for isolation we provide tenant-level prefix caching on dedicated pools which reduces token cost and improves warm-start latencies.
- Latency: Typically lower tail-latency variability for modest traffic due to continuous batching tuned per pool.
- Failure modes: We provide cross-region fallback and model-variant fallbacks.

Private (VPC / customer-managed):
- Control plane: Customer runs a private control plane; Redwood provides connectors and a management plane overlay. Some telemetry will flow through secure channels.
- KV cache: Cache is customer-resident; warm-start stalls possible during cold starts unless we preload prompts and pre-warm KV.
- Latency: Potentially lower inter-node latency inside a VPC but higher variability during on-prem provisioning or autoscale events.
- Failure modes: Customer to own network-level recovery; Redwood can supply runbooks and automated fallback policies but TLDR: operational ownership shifts to the customer.

Ops ask for sizing: share a 7-day hourly RPS trace if you have it (we used your spreadsheet assumptions to approximate), and note peak concurrent chat sessions and average tokens per session. Those numbers materially impact whether you need more nodes for KV capacity vs compute.

— Karthik Iyer
Lead Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Erin / Samir —

Great sync last week. Per our call, I captured the recommended pathing below to keep the pilot moving while preserving an isolation posture for auditing: 

Recommended two-phase approach (minimize time to pilot + preserve auditability):
1) Short pilot on Dedicated with tenant-level isolation (2–4 week ramp): 
   - Reserve conservative Dedicated slate (8 A40-equivalent GPUs) for 4 weeks.
   - Use tenant-level dedicated pools so Copperlane gets billing segregation and isolated KV caching.
   - Redwood provides SOC2 evidence package and a runbook for audit reviewers.
2) Parallel Private gating work (4–10 weeks): 
   - While the pilot runs, Copperlane and Redwood run the Private onboarding checklist. Vivek will coordinate security requirements and AD/identity integration.
   - If Private is required post-pilot, we’ll migrate model workloads using model-variant parity and automated traffic switchovers to minimize downtime.

Estimated resource summary (ballpark monthly):
- Dedicated conservative pilot: 8 A40-equiv | est $46k–$62k/mo (including reserved + infra fee)
- Dedicated aggressive pilot: 24 A40-equiv | est $136k–$185k/mo
- Private platform + infra (conservative footprint): licence + infra ~ $70k–$95k/mo (wide variance depending on cloud markup and whether Copperlane owns accounts)

Deliverables and timeline: 
- Monday: Marissa sends commercial worksheet and SOW options (ETA Oct 12).
- Week 2: Karthik provides the ops runbook and pre-warm checklist.
- Week 3: Vivek and Aditya start security/data-flow scoping if Copperlane opts for Private.

Erin, if that aligns I’ll lock the Dedicated reservation and send an updated SOW with a short pilot acceptance test and a migration appendix.

Thanks —
Ava
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
